chunks: Al-Qasim Muhammad al-Jawhari narrated from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir, who said:

I asked Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام about a freed woman whom my brother had emancipated. She used to serve the maidservants and was among his dependents, and he instructed me to spend on her in a moderate manner.
So he said: “If she remains with the maidservants and continues attending to them, then spend on her and follow his bequest.”

key_terms.أَعْتَقَهَا: he emancipated her and granted her freedom
key_terms.أُنْفِقَ: to spend financially for maintenance and support
key_terms.مُحَرَّرَةٍ: a freed woman, formerly enslaved and then emancipated
key_terms.وَصِيَّتَهُ: his bequest or final instruction to be carried out
key_terms.ٱلْوَسَطِ: moderation; a middle and balanced level of spending

ai.seo_question: Must a person carry out a bequest to support a freed woman who remained in the household?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about carrying out a deceased person's bequest concerning financial support for a freed woman who remained attached to the household in service. The Imam عليه السلام affirms that if her situation remains as described, the instruction to provide for her should be followed.
